trust_decision.summary: A promise created while deserializing must not be settled (resolve/reject) with a thenable, because Promise settlement reads and invokes value.then, which lets a plugin-produced callable be invoked from data-only payloads passed to fromJSON()/fromCrossJSON(); the decision is enforced at each promise-settlement site of the deserializer.

landing_point.why: fromJSON (packages/seroval/src/core/tree/index.ts:120) calls deserializeTop, whose Promise case (packages/seroval/src/core/context/deserializer.ts:826-827) settles the deferred with the deserialized payload at lines 574-578; that is the first place an engineer reading the fromJSON/Promise report would look.

fix_sites.entry_point: fromJSON (packages/seroval/src/core/tree/index.ts:120) - vanilla Promise node built by parsePromise in packages/seroval/src/core/context/async-parser.ts:355-377

fromCrossJSON (packages/seroval/src/core/cross/index.ts:177) - PromiseConstructor/PromiseSuccess/PromiseFailure nodes produced by the streaming cross parser, packages/seroval/src/core/context/sync-parser.ts:474-558
fix_sites.module_kind: cross/streaming deserializer promise-settlement handler (two formerly separate handlers merged, fix.diff:131-168)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: packages/seroval/src/core/cross/index.ts:177 (fromCrossJSON) reaching the deferred settlement code at packages/seroval/src/core/context/deserializer.ts:641-661; that node family (PromiseConstructor/PromiseSuccess/PromiseFailure) is only produced by the cross streaming parser, packages/seroval/src/core/context/sync-parser.ts:474-558

O3_reason_to_dismiss: fromCrossJSON is handed a bare SerovalNode plus a caller-owned refs map by the same application's worker/SSR transport, so a solver can argue it is not the untrusted-JSON surface the advisory names and leave the deferred settlement path alone.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A rejected promise whose reason happens to be a thenable must still reject with that value: reject() never assimilates, only resolve()/fulfil does, so a payload whose PromiseFailure (or Promise node with s=0) carries a plugin-produced object with a callable `then` is legitimate and must arrive as the rejection reason rather than throw SerovalMalformedNodeError.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: packages/seroval/src/core/context/deserializer.ts:574-578; the published fix puts the same guard in front of both branches (fix.diff:121-123) and in front of the merged PromiseFailure branch (fix.diff:161-167)

O6_input_shapes: Promise node whose deserialized payload (node.f) is a thenable - guard at fix.diff:121-123
PromiseConstructor deferred + PromiseSuccess node whose payload (node.a[1]) is a thenable - guard at fix.diff:161-162
PromiseConstructor deferred + PromiseFailure node whose payload (node.a[1]) is a thenable - same merged guard, branch chosen by node.t (fix.diff:164-168)
thenable produced by a plugin node nested anywhere in the payload, surfaced at packages/seroval/src/core/context/deserializer.ts:609, invisible to any earlier check
object whose `then` key is not callable (not a thenable by spec), which must still pass - hence the typeof value.then === 'function' half of the predicate (fix.diff:105-112)

O7_producer.where: packages/seroval/src/core/context/deserializer.ts:609 - deserializePlugin hands plugin-supplied data to plugin.deserialize, the only way fromJSON can turn nodes into non-data values such as callables (e.g. packages/plugins/web/abort-signal.ts:52-54 returns PROMISE_TO_ABORT_SIGNAL, a function)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Mirror guard on the code-generating side: serializePromise emits `PROMISE_SUCCESS(<value>)` / `Promise.resolve().then(function(){return ref})`, which assimilates the same way once the emitted string is evaluated.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the same mechanism in the other direction and shares the resolver helpers, so a maintainer fixing settlement would plausibly guard the emitter too (the pinned tree even keeps a snapshot for exactly that expression, packages/seroval/test/__snapshots__/promise.test.ts.snap:3-5).

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Thenable guard on the promise settlements inside ASYNC_ITERATOR_CONSTRUCTOR (temp.s({done:false,value}) at line 198, temp.s({done:true,value}) at line 215, finalize at line 187).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This is the second place where deserializer-created promises are settled from streamed values, reached from deserializeAsyncIteratorFactoryInstance (packages/seroval/src/core/context/deserializer.ts:674-682); a maintainer auditing settlements would find it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Reject thenable/callable plugin results at plugin dispatch (for example a fromJSON option that refuses plugin output which is a callable or a thenable).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: deserializePlugin is the only producer of callables in the data-only path, so a maintainer could reasonably put the defence at the producer instead of at each settlement site.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A catalog plugin whose deserialized value is a thenable (for example a lazy/query-style wrapper plugin returning an object with a `then` method).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: packages/plugins/web is a catalog of wrapper plugins (AbortSignal, ReadableStream, Response, Request); adding a promise-like wrapper plugin there is exactly the shape that produces the hidden thenable.

O9_family: CWE-843 type confusion - thenable assimilation of a plugin-produced value during deserialization (untrusted data reaches a callable invocation)
